title: JSON
body:
*JavaScript Object Notation* — a text format for structured data, and the default way APIs exchange it. The syntax is a subset of JavaScript object literals: objects in `{}`, arrays in `[]`, plus strings, numbers, booleans and `null`.

```json
{ "id": 44, "name": "Hamilton", "wins": 105, "active": true }
```

It's stricter than JS object syntax — keys must be double-quoted strings, trailing commas are illegal, and comments aren't allowed. Crucially it holds **data only**: no functions, no dates (they become strings), no `undefined`.

In the browser, `JSON.parse(text)` turns it into a JS object and `JSON.stringify(obj)` turns one back into text. `response.json()` in [[Fetch]] does the parse for you, returning a [[Promise]] because the body may still be arriving. Being text, it's also language-neutral — which is why a Python or Ruby backend and a [[JavaScript]] frontend can agree on it.
